---
title: "Rundial"
---

Sundial is the variant calling step for ONT. It uses Minimap2 for alignment, BCFTools for pileup and then python for filtering the the VCF and producing a consensus fasta.

Rundial is a rust upgrade which replaces the python code with rust.

github: [GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/sundial ](https://github.com/GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/sundial) and [GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/rundial](https://github.com/GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/rundial)

# Thresholds

Main parameters summarised below. See code for details.

## Minimap2

The alignment is produced with no secondary alignments but otherwise using default ont settings

## BCFTools

BCFTools mpileup is used for the initial variant calling. It is run with ploidy 1 (so GT is a single value) and the multiallelic caller mode (`-m`)

All sites with depth==0 are filtered for the gvcf for consistency

## Clair3

As an alternative, the machine learning approach for variant calling can be done with Clair3. This also produces a VCF (like bcftools). It requires that an appropriate Clair3 model is selected based on the basecaller used during sequencing.

Clair3 does not produce a gvcf and so BCFTools is still run in order to call nulls at other sites as appropriate.

## Filtering the VCF

Various filters are applied to the VCF before making a consensus. These are determined by the `filter_params.yml` or `clair3_filter_params.yml` files. These are used to mark sites which are low quality for various reasons:

- Low depth / Low high quality read depth
- Low mapping quality
- Strand bias - When almost all read support is on just one strand
- Strand mismatch - When the different strands support different base calls.
- Min fractional support - when not a high enough proportion of the reads support the call.
- Min idv - min number of reads supporting an indel call
- min imf - min fraction of reads supporting an indel, as bcftools calculates (seems a little different to simply allele depth)

During this step, the GT for each row is set based on the high quality read depth (rather than bcftools internal logic), and converted to a ploidy 2 format for consistency and to allow het calls (where read support allows).

## Consensus

The filtered VCF is then used to make the consensus fasta, and a simplified VCF file.

- Filtered sites are set to N
- Passed SNPs are applied
- Het SNPs are set to Z in the fasta
- Passed indels are only used if they don’t overlap with snps or higher quality indels
    - NOTE: they currently still get output to the vcf for transparency
- Deletions are applied by converting deleted bases to `-`
- Insertions are applied to the indel.fasta only.

The resulting main VCF contains all variants, all passed indels (even if not applied due to overlaps), and all null sites.
